claims.text: An enhanced-sampling molecular-dynamics framework combining metadynamics or umbrella sampling with thermodynamic integration can determine melting temperature, enthalpy and entropy of fusion, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed framework is applicable across a broad HEA compositional range.
The method would start from solid HEAs with well-characterized compositional distributions.
Calibration on simpler alloy systems supports application of the method to HEAs.
Metadynamics or umbrella sampling can overcome free-energy barriers associated with melting.
The simulations should be conducted near the melting transition under controlled pressure or volume.
Applicability across diverse HEA compositions requires near-equilibrium phase-transition behavior.
The relevant mediator is the solid-liquid free-energy difference, accompanied by latent heat and a discontinuous volume change at melting.
Enhanced sampling drives the simulated system across the free-energy barrier between solid and liquid phases.
Thermodynamic integration can reliably compute the solid-liquid free-energy difference.
Latent-heat signatures and volume discontinuities obtained from the simulations directly yield melting properties.
Predicted melting temperatures, latent heats, and volume changes will be within roughly 5–10% of high-precision calorimetric measurements.
Predicted liquid-phase thermodynamic properties will have similar quantitative fidelity relative to established benchmarks.
CALPHAD-based computation is an existing approach used to explore HEA composition spaces.
Experimental calorimetry, CALPHAD, and conventional atomistic simulation often compromise between efficiency and universality across HEA composition space.
Extreme compositional heterogeneity or significant nonequilibrium melting effects may limit the method.
The method assumes equilibrium thermodynamics dominate and may require recalibration when kinetic effects are pronounced.
Local compositional fluctuations and nonequilibrium kinetics create uncertainty in performance over the full HEA composition space.
The approach can be tested by comparing simulations with simultaneous DSC and volumetric measurements on the same HEAs across multiple compositions.
Consistent deviations exceeding approximately 10% across a significant HEA composition range, or failure to reproduce latent-heat and volume discontinuities, would falsify the approach.
